data.content_ref: inline:The proposed 'contradiction' is misframed: a vulnerability window from patch-synchronization lag is an operational cost or trade-off, not a logical incompatibility with resilience. Resilience claims can coexist with temporary exposure windows — a system can still recover from or withstand failures despite imperfect patching. The refutation condition is also too narrow: showing that sync lag causes a vulnerability window exceeding the benefit of avoiding shared runtime may weaken the resilience case, but it does not refute the *contradiction* relation itself, since the two claims (coordination decay vs. diversity benefit) address different dimensions of the same property and are better characterized as a tension or trade-off than a strict contradiction.
